method: weight = distinct authors x (1 + 0.5 x (networks - 1)); rising = conversation posts in the last day / daily average over 7 days; signal (0-100, per window) = 0.40 x pct(voices) + 0.25 x pct(reach) + 0.20 x pct(rising) + 0.15 x pct(engagement excl. Reddit); pct(x) = share of the other topics on the map with a strictly lower value (ties share the lower rank; a zero value scores 0); reach = distinct networks other than newsletters and Official + distinct newsletters; voices exclude Official feeds; rising is the node-level 24h-vs-7d ratio, a missing rising or a ratio below 1 scores 0; engagement = sum of log(1 + score + comments) over matching posts outside Reddit (Reddit archive scores are ingestion snapshots). A heuristic for ordering attention, not a measure of truth or importance; reach_pct (per window) = mean of the five highest item percentiles among the items matching the topic; an item's percentile is taken within its own type and window: posts per network (HN points, Mastodon favourites + boosts, Lobsters score, Bluesky likes + reposts; Reddit excluded, its archive scores are ingestion snapshots), papers (HF upvotes), repos (stars gained in the window); raw counts are never summed across types; organic (30d live conversation by named authors): burst = share of posts in the densest 6 hours; dupe = share of posts (5+ words) whose 5-word-shingle Jaccard with a post by a different author is >= 0.6; single_topic = share of authors with 2+ stored posts whose posts all match the topic; link_push = largest share of posts pointing at one target URL; repos = anti-noise flags on matching tracker repos; dossier = HYPE coordination assessment. Label: too few posts (< 10); a signal fires at burst >= 0.5, dupe >= 0.2, single_topic >= 0.5 (5+ authors), link_push >= 0.3 (5+ posts), repos stars>activity on half of 3+ repos, dossier disclosed or measured coordination; strong = two signals or burst >= 0.7, dupe >= 0.4, link_push >= 0.5. Signals, not proof; new (the default ranking): two legs, each a percentile among topics that qualify for it, and a topic ranks by the higher one. talk = lift of the topic's share of posts in the last 7 days over its share in days 8-30, on the deep networks only (live networks with posts on >= 70% of the baseline days and >= 50 baseline posts; shallower archives cannot show what is normal yet), baseline smoothed by +1 post; it qualifies with >= 2 deep-network posts this week, >= 5 voices and >= 2 networks in 7 days. build = count of tracker repos matching the topic (a repo in a tracker paradigm counts only for that paradigm's theme) that were born in the last 30 days; it qualifies with >= 3 born repos that are >= half of its repos (a new wave, not an old field). always-on = mentioned on the deep networks on >= 60% of the baseline days with talk lift < 2: big but not news; its talk leg does not count. Lift is relative to what we sampled, not to the whole internet; stories (last 7 days): an event is a cluster of posts. HN, Lobsters, newsletter and official items seed clusters and join when they share a canonical target link or idf-weighted title overlap >= 0.45 with two shared uncommon words (each in < 2% of the window's posts); posts naming the same model version or emerging name join one story; Reddit, Mastodon and Bluesky posts attach to their release or the best seed at >= 0.40; unmatched chatter joins at >= 0.55 and stands alone only with 5+ voices. covered = seeded by HN, Lobsters, a newsletter or a lab/vendor feed, or carried by a newsletter; otherwise it is chatter not yet in the press. pain = share of its post titles that read as a complaint, outage or support problem (keyword list); kind = news when covered, else pain when pain >= 0.5, else chatter. Headlines prefer statements over questions and complaints. A newsletter carries a story when its item names all of the story's key words (up to three uncommon words shared by its editorial posts). heat = (2 x log2(1 + voices) + networks outside newsletters/official + 1.5 x newsletters carrying it + 1 if a lab or vendor posted it + log10(1 + HN points)) x 0.5^(hours since the newest post / 48). id = "s:" + first 12 hex of sha1("release:" + topic id when the story is about one named release, else the canonical target link of its earliest editorial post, else that post's URL); when two stories name the same release, the one whose earliest editorial post is earliest (then the lower key) keeps the release key and the other takes its earliest editorial post's key, with "#" appended while that key is still taken, so ids are unique and do not swap as posts arrive. Reddit, X, LinkedIn, YouTube and Telegram posts (and Mastodon posts without a logged-out render check passed in the last 7 days) count but are never shown: no title, author, link or score; a headline that would be one reads the earliest shown post's title, else the topic label, else "<network> discussion, title not shown". Conversation-network authors are never published. refs = the GitHub repositories and arXiv papers (arxiv.org, huggingface.co/papers, alphaxiv.org ids) that the story's shown posts link to, by post URL or target link; a count-only post's link is not read
projects_note: projects: live sampled feeds only (no tracker, no dossier); voices = distinct (network, author) pairs, nets = distinct networks; 0 means no matching post in our sampled feeds, not zero attention
coverage: Sampled feeds, not internet-wide totals: HN stories above 20 points, the Lobsters AI tag, nine Mastodon hashtags on mastodon.social, ten AI subreddits via the arctic-shift public archive (up to 1,000 newest posts per subreddit per run, so busy subreddits reach back about a week), twelve public AI newsletter feeds (the digest end point), lab and vendor announcement feeds (the Official network: where launches originate), tracker papers and repos, and the static HYPE research dossier. Bluesky appears only when an app password is configured. X appears only through the static dossier; it is not collected live.
Topics come from a reviewable lexicon (topics_lexicon.json), automatic model-version names, and capitalised phrases used by at least three distinct authors (marked emerging).
